    FACILITATOR REFERENCE

    RoverLens · Study guide

    An interactive demonstration of the framework in Mind the Middle Layer: A Requirements-Driven Study of Wrong Mental Models in LLM-Agent-Controlled Robots, Md Akib Haider, working draft (2026).

    This is an experimental apparatus, not a completed study. No participant results are prefilled or claimed.

    A short demonstration

    1. Choose a scenario and run it in interface A (opaque).
    2. Switch to B (transparent) and repeat the same command and fault.
    3. Compare what can be inferred about capabilities, context, and the failure source.
    4. Open “Inspect episode” to trace command → code → checks → flash → feedback.

    Running a participant session

    Choose the condition and scenario before enabling Participant view. This hides the library, fault labels, mode switch, guide and technical trace. It is a presentation boundary, not an access-control system. Configure between tasks when the participant is not looking.

    WM4 needs two actions: send the full movement command, then send “Do that again”. The controlled fault expires the agent’s context immediately before the follow-up. Repeat both steps in the other condition.

    Use a balanced A→B / B→A order across participants and reset between participants. Obtain the consent and institutional approval described in the paper before collecting study data. Reflections and logs remain in this tab’s memory until exported; refreshing or resetting clears them. Export before resetting. The export contains raw commands and optional reflections, so avoid names or personal details.

    Requirements, implemented as simulations

    Taxonomy and scope

    Simulation limits

    Deterministic English command matching stands in for an LLM. Firmware text and three validation checks are illustrative, not a real compiler or safety certification. Motion is a visual approximation. WM1 and WM5 are documented only. The optional WM7 update changes the allowed motion duration from 5 s to 3 s. No microphone, network API, physical robot, participant scoring, or inferred diagnosis is used.
